source.section: PDF page 23, Table E (Head of Household, more than 25,000 to 25,500: .60) and Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 7-10; PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 25,200.00 = 25,200.00. Federal taxable income = 25,200.00 - 23,625.00 standard deduction = 1,575.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 25,200.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 25,200.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 0.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 0.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 25,200.00 - 0.00 = 25,200.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 25,200.00; Line 2 Table A (Head of Household): Connecticut AGI 25,200.00 is not more than 38,000.00, exemption 19,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 25,200.00 - 19,000.00 = 6,200.00. Line 4 Table B (Head of Household schedule) on 6,200.00: 6,200.00 x 0.02 = 124.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 25,200.00 is not more than 78,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 168,000.00); Line 7 = 124.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.60 (Connecticut AGI 25,200.00 is in the Head of Household band more than 25,000.00 and not more than 25,500.00; the projection's step rate 0.60 over 25,000); Line 9 = 124.00 x 0.60 = 74.40, less than the Line 7 tax, so all of it is allowed. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 124.00 - 74.40 = 49.60 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: a Table E band inside the phase-down (neither the full .75 nor the long .10 plateau), read from the step's rate field.
